content.body:
## About the Voluntary Disclosure Program

The City of Arvada is a business-friendly municipality and is committed to helping businesses achieve compliance with their sales and use tax obligations. While the City of Arvada does not have a formal **Voluntary Disclosure Agreement (VDA)** program due to potential conflicts with the Arvada Municipal Code, it recognizes good-faith efforts to reach compliance. Businesses seeking to become compliant should submit a VDA application, through which the City typically waives penalties on prior taxes if they are paid within 30 days of the assessment date.

### Lookback Period

The general lookback period for voluntary disclosures is **36 months (3 years)**. This period may be extended if a business has collected Arvada taxes but failed to remit them, as businesses are not permitted to retain any collected Arvada tax.

### Process for Applying

Businesses will need to complete the [Voluntary Disclosure Application](https://arvada.form.transform.civicplus.com/62076), which will require the following information:

- A letter requesting the Voluntary Disclosure – This letter should include information such as:
  - A description of the taxpayer’s activities and the date the activities began;
  - An estimate of the Arvada tax liability for previous tax periods;
  - A disclosure with respect to whether the company has or has not collected the relevant taxes;
  - A representation that the company has not been previously contacted by the City of Arvada;
  - A representation that the failure to file is not the result of fraud or gross negligence on the part of the company.
- Work papers supporting the taxable sales, sales tax and periods covered.  The sales data should include delivery addresses so that they can be verified.
- City of Arvada license number – Information about applying for a business license is available on our [Business Licenses](/253) page.

The VDA amount (taxes and interest) will be posted to the businesses Arvada sales tax account. This will be considered a one-time catch-up return in which no penalty will be assessed if payment is made within 30 days of the assessment date.
